set.approach: From the parking lot at the former Old Man site in Franconia Notch, take the Greenleaf Trail, which climbs toward the AMC Greenleaf Hut. A little before Eagle Pass, once the grade eases, a small cairn on your left marks a climbers' path heading steeply up. Bear left at each split, staying under the trees and clear of the talus field to the right. The route begins on the stone patio immediately to the left of Wunderbub.
set.descent_text: Descent is by lowering back to the ground from the top anchor, or in two stages by lowering from the intermediate anchor, the Wunderbub anchor, first.

review.notes: Route page states start and lowering; rope lengths left out.

set.approach: From the parking lot at the former Old Man site in Franconia Notch, take the Greenleaf Trail, which climbs toward the AMC Greenleaf Hut. A little before Eagle Pass, once the grade eases, a small cairn on your left marks a climbers' path heading steeply up. Bear left at each split, staying under the trees and clear of the talus field to the right. The route is at the extreme left end of the Main Cliff. It begins at the head of a steep gully, right under a huge hanging corner up the wall.
set.descent_text: Descent is by rappel. The big hanging roof leaves the rappeller hanging free, so the rappel cannot go straight back to the first-pitch anchor; use the bolted rappel station lower down in the gully, off to the right of that first anchor.

review.notes: Route page states location and descent.

set.approach: Start from the rescue cache on the floor of Tuckerman Ravine and bushwhack across, keeping the Remi Bourdage memorial boulder on your left. Work over the boulder field to the clear gully left of Lion's Head (as you face it) and follow it up to the height of a small gendarme-shaped feature. A short bushwhack then contours to the foot of that feature and an obvious launch pad where the climbing starts.
set.descent_text: The route ends just below the summit of Lion's Head. From there walk down the Lion's Head Trail, which is the trail you are standing on.

review.notes: Route page states location, summit top-out and walk-down.

set.approach: The Upper Face sits above the huge tree ledge on Mt. Willard and is normally reached by climbing one of the Main Face routes. Thor is toward the right-hand end of the upper tier, a short way left of Salespitch. The start is easy to recognize by a homemade bolt just above the ground, under a large beech and on top of a pointed rock.
set.descent_text: The Upper Face is descended by the hiking path down to the road, so park with that in mind.

review.notes: Approach from route and area pages; walk-down from the area page (medium).

set.approach: Buttress 3 is the last of the Boott Spur Buttresses, the right-most one seen from the far side of Tuckerman Ravine. Hike the Boott Spur Trail and leave it before the Boott Spur summit to traverse in to the base of the buttresses.

review.notes: Approach only; no descent stated.

set.approach: Park at the Cannon Tramway, walk through the tunnel and follow the Greenleaf Trail to a cairn, then take the approach gully used for the Eaglet and Flatiron. At the talus field bear left, as you would for the Flatiron. Close to the bottom of the last approach slab, a path falls away left beyond a big boulder to the base of a short buttress, which is climbed at easy fifth class, followed by a short bulge. Move back right past loose blocks to the lone bolt that starts Route 66, the first route on the wall.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the two-bolt anchor on top of the buttress.

review.notes: Approach from the area page; start and rappel anchor from the route page. Rope count left out.

set.approach: Billings Fold is the sunny slab directly below the summit of Mount Monadnock, off the Smiths Summit Trail. The traverse starts up Stemming Corner.
set.descent_text: At the end of the wall, either top out or downclimb the gully, which is somewhat awkward.

review.notes: Route page states the start and the end options; area page the location.

set.approach: Follow the paved path from the parking area at the north end of Cannon Cliff to the large boulder on the right that has a sign across the trail; swing around it through the trees and climb the talus to the Moby Grape routes. The route takes the clear chimney at the right-hand edge of the Moby buttress.

review.notes: Approach only; the route ends at Moby's anchor and no descent is stated.

set.approach: Park at the northern end of the Wapack Trail and hike south on it to the summit of North Pack. From there head east on the Cliff Trail, passing the Carolyn's Trail junction, until you reach the top of the cliff with the Pack Monadnock fire tower in view. Walk down and around the cliff through the scree field to its base. AMC Corner is the obvious corner.
set.descent_text: The top of the cliff carries no bolts or rappel stations. The way down is the walk around the cliff through the scree field, and a rappel from natural anchors is a second option.

review.notes: Crag page for approach and the descent; route page for the line.
